question.text: For a short dipole placed at origin $O$, the dipole moment $P$ is along $x$-axis, as shown in the figure. If the electric potential and electric field at A are $\mathrm{V}_0$ and $\mathrm{E}_0$, respectively, then the correct combination of the electric potential and electric field, respectively, at point $B$ on the $y$-axis is given by

solution.text:
At point $A$ (axial)
$\left|E_0\right|=\frac{2 k_p}{r^3}, V_0=\frac{k_p}{r^2}$

At point $B$ (equatorial)
$\begin{aligned}
& |E|=\frac{k_p}{(2 r)^3}=\frac{E_0}{16} \\
& V=0
\end{aligned}$
